neighbours.label: The end of the condition in a 'do X and (you) Y' conditional ('any longer than that and you risk', 'mention it to an old hacker and they'll'), the slot right before the consequence 'and'
fire: Stir the sauce for any more than five minutes and it will start to stick to the pan.
Water the cactus more than once a week and you risk rotting its roots.
Leave the gate open for longer than an hour and the goats will wander off.
Give a toddler a cardboard box and you will see an afternoon of happy play.
Push the engine any harder than that and you could crack a cylinder.
Skip a single day of practice and you will notice it at the next lesson.
Add a pinch of salt to the caramel, and you will taste the difference at once.
Wait any later than noon and you will find every table at the cafe taken.
quiet: If you stir the sauce too long, it will start to stick to the pan.
Cacti that are watered too often tend to rot at the roots.
When the gate is left open, the goats usually wander off.
Toddlers often play happily for hours with a cardboard box.
Running the engine too hard can crack a cylinder.
Daily practice makes a clear difference by the next lesson.
A pinch of salt makes caramel taste richer, which most cooks know.
By noon most tables at the cafe are usually taken.

predictions: The last word of the condition in 'X and you will Y' 0.2-0.5, highest for 'any longer/more than N and'; the same content as an if-clause or plain statement under 0.05.
notes: Card: top peaks on the word before ', and you will see', 'and you risk', 'and they're sure to', 'and you'd get'; the - pole promotes ' and'. Probe: 'any longer than ten minutes and you will burn' 0.513, 'Add a little patience to this recipe, and you will see' 0.214, 'Say his name to any old sailor and they will' 0.159, 'any two finches and you would' 0.069; if-clause and plain versions <= 0.010. 'apples and pears at the market' 0.116 (list 'and' leaks a little). Mid-strength, expect a weak hold or a fail on median.
